newsitem.title: USA: El Abra ramping up to above design capacity-Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: El Abra ramping up to above design capacity-Cyprus.

text.p: Cyprus Amax's new El Abra copper mine in Chile will hit above-design capacity output by the end of 1997, its first full year of operation, the company's chairman, president and CEO Milton Ward said.
"We think that we will be at full design rate by the end of the second quarter, and we think we will be above design rate in the second half," Ward told an analysts teleconference briefing Thursday.
"For startup year, that's excellent," Ward added.
The mine has been scheduled to produce 225,000 tonnes a year.
El Abra is 51 percent owned by Cyprus and 49 percent owned by Codelco, the state owned Chilean copper company.
The new mine and SX/EW project produced just under 100 million pounds of copper (45,360 tonnes) in the first quarter of this year.
Some minor, startup problems have been encountered such as cathodes sticking to starter sheets, faulty seals, and coping with three-day lightning storms in the desert.
"But there is nothing abnormal," Cyprus officials said.
The drought hitting Chile is having no effect on El Abra, the company said.
El Abra's production helped Cyprus increase first quarter copper production by 40 percent to 241 million lb compared to the first quarter of last year.
